Welcome and thank you for taking time to visit our website
At Woodlands Meed we believe you will find an incredibly positive and supportive environment, within both the school and college. These are happy and friendly places to learn, work and build the best possible future.
Each student is offered individualised care and learning, while belonging to an inclusive, understanding and rewarding community. Our dedicated teaching staff all possess skills across a wide range of expertise. Also, we benefit from a strong multi-disciplinary team of medical therapists, providing excellent care for all: speech and language therapy, occupational therapy, special school nurses and physiotherapy. Working together with the knowledgeable and experienced educational staff, they provide a highly personalised and creative curriculum, encouraging all students to achieve their full potential.
Located in the heart of Burgess Hill, Woodlands Meed welcomes students aged between 2 and 19 years, who live within a one hour travel time. If you would like to see our exciting and vibrant school or college for yourself, we would love to take you for a tour and show you all we have to offer. Please email sfernandes@woodlandsmeed.co.uk or phone 01444 244133 to speak to one of our team and arrange a tour.
Adam RowlandHeadteacher

Personal Careers Guidance
Students in years 11 and 13 will have access to impartial 1:1 personal careers advice and guidance undertaken by an independent careers company.
Students are invited to their interview by letter, a copy of the letter and information leaflet is also sent to parents/carers. Where possible the interviews take place before a students’ Annual Review where they discuss the student's strengths, the type of job they would like to have and how to work towards achieving their goals.
To prepare the students for their interview they will have the opportunity to update their Vocational Profile and attend a short workshop with a careers advisor.
Following the interview a written report along with a list of actions to enable the student to get closer to their goals will be produced. These actions are tracked by the MJC and the class teacher.

SEND and Inclusion Reviews
We are very excited to be working alongside the West Sussex SEND and Inclusion Advisors to deliver SEND Reviews in the Mid Sussex area. SEND Reviews are invaluable to schools and are a way of getting an external view of the SEND provision within a school, not to be judgemental, but curious and pose questions to work with the school to help develop this area. The aims of the review will help you to:
The review will help your school align with the West Sussex Inclusion Framework, the Ordinarily Available Inclusive Practice Guide, and the OFSTED Inspection Framework.
"Our SEND review with the Meeds SEND Alliance was a positive and informative experience, helping us to identify and celebrate the strengths in our provision and practice and to highlight ways forward in areas where we have more to do. A supportive and reflective experience."
Helen Williamson - Head at Billingshurst Primary

Careers Events
We host and plan a number of exciting Careers Events throughout the year including the Woodlands Meed Business Brunch and the Woodlands Meed Careers and Transitions Fair, as well as a variety of activities during National Careers Week.
Business Brunch
Woodlands Meed have hosted several Networking Brunches as part of their strategy to engage with the local business community.
These meetings give us the opportunity to share great news about students’ progress into the workplace, our development of the Supported Internship programme and a call to action to engage with the college in a number of different ways –as a guest speaker, hosting visits, providing work experience, and fundraising.
Inspire Café, our student led enterprise provided the catering for these events, giving employers the opportunity to meet students and see the potential contribution they can make to their workforce.
Team Brit
In July 2024, a group of students got the opportunity to visit Team Brit which gives people with disabilities the chance to compete with able-bodied drivers in national motor racing events.
The students got great insight into STEM challenges of adapting vehicles to use hand control technology.
This visit was a reward trip for great teamwork on a work experience project, spending a half-term providing a valued service to parents and children of our neighbouring primary school.
Time for Transition
The Meed’s Job Club were delighted to welcome a variety of transitions services to college during Spring term parents evening.

The Meeds SEND Alliance
Welcome
The Meeds SEND Alliance is a support service for schools and their families of young people with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND) in West Sussex.​ The Meeds SEND Alliance is led by Jan James of Woodlands Meed. Jan is supported by Louise (Administration) and Andrea (Finance). We offer support to both member and non-member schools of the Meeds SEND Alliance.
The Alliance aims to improve outcomes for children with SEND and supports schools and families by:
Developing networks between schools and other service providers​
Sharing resources, skills and expertise​
Providing an outreach service for schools
Assessing and meeting the needs for training​
Signposting to other organisations and support​
Providing peer support for Inclusion Leaders​
Contributing to the Local Offer of provision for young people with SEND​
Providing support for families of young people with SEND
If you are interested in becoming a member or finding out more about what we do, get in touch here.
We look forward to hearing from you!

SEND Information
Our SEN Information Report is published with our policies to assist parents, carers and others with an overview of our special needs provision at Woodlands Meed.
Our classroom staff all have an interest and commitment to work with children who have special educational needs and disabilities, and our Deputy Headteachers Chris Carter (school site) and Gillian Barton (college site) are responsible for managing specialist provision for our learners and liaising with the NHS therapists who work at Woodlands Meed.
Woodlands Meed contributes to the Local Offer in its provision for special needs education and in leading the Meeds SEND Alliance to support families and other schools.

At Woodlands Meed, the curriculum is designed to provide our pupils with opportunities to gain relevant skills, knowledge and understanding.
We aim to ensure that our pupils become well-rounded, happy individuals who are ready for the next stage of their lives.
"Since transferring from mainstream to Woodlands Meed, James has made real progress in both learning and making friends with thanks to all the support he gets from all his class teachers who understand his needs well. Because of this he has settled in really well and as his parents, we look forward to the continued progress we know he is capable of making now that he is in the right supportive environment."
